xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5278: CLIProxy: route new sessions to the account that resets soonest, and show pooled account usage

plan.title: CLIProxy: route new sessions to the account that resets soonest, and show pooled account usage
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: CLIProxy round-robins requests across a provider's accounts, so quota an account has not used when its window resets is lost. Overdeck also gives operators no view of the pooled accounts' usage, and today the management API only works because the operator added it to config.extra.yaml by hand.
narratives.Proposal: Without forking CLIProxy 7.3.16: generate session-affinity and a localhost-only management API in config.yaml; keep operator fields when the Codex bridge rewrites its auth file; add a leaf pool reader that lists accounts and reads Codex/Claude usage through the management api-call endpoint; a host-only controller ranks each provider's accounts by soonest weekly reset every 5 minutes (only when a provider has 2+ enabled accounts) and writes CLIProxy per-account priority; a read-only GET /api/cliproxy/accounts and a Settings → Providers panel show the pool.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Redeeming Codex reset credits, calling /v0/management/reset-quota, or any 'Use reset' button
- Upgrading or forking CLIProxy (stay on v7.3.16)
- Exposing the management API beyond localhost (allow-remote stays false; no Tailscale exposure; no MANAGEMENT_PASSWORD env var)
- Signing Claude or any other accounts into the proxy
- Ranking providers other than codex and claude
- A setting to turn the controller off, or a route-scopes.ts row for the new route
- Persisting the pool snapshot to disk or the read model
- Writes from GET /api/cliproxy/accounts (it never PATCHes priorities)
- Tests that contact port 8317 or any upstream provider

autoDecisions.summary: Planned from the operator-revised PRD on main (aae9223552c): read-only route via readPoolSnapshot, sync ensureConfigFile deleted with no null-key writer, usage reads only when a provider has 2+ enabled accounts, PATCH persistence proven by the checkpoint item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator sent these revisions during planning; they are the authoritative input.

autoDecisions.summary: ensureConfigFileAsync compares parsed YAML with a bcrypt secret-key masked instead of raw text (PRD Decision 11, NFR-5).
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified at v7.3.16 and on the live config: CLIProxy hashes the plaintext key and writes it back, also dropping blank lines, so a text compare rewrites config.yaml on every Gemini spawn and triggers a reload. MANAGEMENT_PASSWORD would enable remote access; Overdeck-side bcrypt needs a new dependency.

autoDecisions.summary: When config.extra.yaml defines remote-management, Overdeck generates no key and reads the management-key file (PRD Decision 10).
autoDecisions.rationale: FR-2 says so, and generating a key there would write a file that does not match the operator's secret.

autoDecisions.summary: The accounts route serves its cached snapshot for at most 5 minutes and the panel shows the snapshot age (PRD Decision 13, NFR-6).
autoDecisions.rationale: With one account per provider the controller never refreshes the snapshot, so without a max age the panel would show the first read forever.

autoDecisions.summary: The PATCH checkpoint is its own spike item that blocks the pool reader, and records its result in the PRD.
autoDecisions.rationale: setAccountPriority's body depends on the result; a committed PRD section keeps the evidence where review can read it.

autoDecisions.summary: Bridge tests live in tests/lib/cliproxy-bridge.test.ts rather than cliproxy-config.test.ts.
autoDecisions.rationale: Separate test files keep the two items' diffs independent; they still share src/lib/cliproxy.ts, which an edge serializes.

metadata.sizeJustification: The issue scopes one feature (generated config, bridge fix, pool reader, controller, route, panel) whose 19 files span few real code areas: src/lib, one server route file, one Settings section, and docs. The subsystem count also counts test and doc directories. The panel and route only make sense on top of the pool reader, and the DAG already lets independent items run in parallel slots, so sibling issues would add review overhead without parallelism.

items.title: Generate session-affinity and localhost management-API blocks in CLIProxy config.yaml

narrative.Action: PRD work item 1 steps 1-6 and Decisions 10-11. In src/lib/cliproxy.ts add getCliproxyManagementKeyPath(), async ensureManagementKey() (randomBytes(24).toString('hex'), mode 0o600, reuse a non-empty existing file), exported async readManagementKey() (null when missing/empty), extraDefinesTopLevelKey(extra,key) (regex-escaped '^key:' multiline). Change buildCliproxyConfig to emit the routing block (strategy round-robin, session-affinity true, ttl "1h") unless extra defines routing, and the remote-management block (allow-remote false, secret-key = serializeYamlString(key)) unless extra defines remote-management. In ensureConfigFileAsync: if extra defines remote-management, generate no key and emit no block; otherwise await ensureManagementKey() and pass it (never null on the generated path). Convert startCliproxy line 631 to await ensureConfigFileAsync() and delete the sync ensureConfigFile, plus ensureDirs/readBridgedGeminiApiKey if they become unused. Replace the text-equality check with exported configsEquivalent(existing, generated): equal text => true; else parse both with yaml.parse, and if the existing remote-management.secret-key matches /^\$2[aby]\$/ set both secret-key values to one sentinel, then return isDeepStrictEqual; parse error => false. Update the module header (lines 1-16) to mention the generated routing and remote-management blocks. New test file tests/lib/cliproxy-config.test.ts mocks os.homedir() to a temp dir following tests/lib/cliproxy-spawn.test.ts; it never touches ~/.overdeck or port 8317.

Pool reader: list CLIProxy accounts and read Codex/Claude usage through api-call

metadata.parallelSafeReason: It creates two new files (src/lib/cliproxy-pool.ts and its test) that no other item edits; it only reads exports from src/lib/cliproxy.ts after config-affinity-mgmt lands.

narrative.Action: PRD work item 3. New leaf module src/lib/cliproxy-pool.ts importing only ./cliproxy.js (CLIPROXY_BASE_URL, readManagementKey, CliproxyError) and Node built-ins. Export the PoolWindow/PoolAccount/PoolSnapshot types exactly as in the PRD, plus listPoolAccounts() (local GET auth-files only, no upstream calls), readPool(), setAccountPriority(name, priority). Use fetch with AbortController + setTimeout(15_000), never AbortSignal.timeout. Upstream calls go through POST /v0/management/api-call with $TOKEN$ headers; at most 4 concurrent; codex and claude parse rules, labels, weekly window and exhausted rule from the PRD glossary and steps 4-6. setAccountPriority uses the mechanism the verify-priority-patch checkpoint recorded (PATCH by default; temp-file + rename rewrite of the auth JSON if the checkpoint says PATCH does not persist). Never log or return the management key, tokens, or upstream body text. Module header explains the job and the no-secrets rule. Tests stub globalThis.fetch with vi.fn routed by URL/body; fake timers for the timeout case.

items.title: Given no management-key file, when readPool() runs, then it returns managementAvailable false and an empty accounts list without calling fetch

Given auth-files lists one codex account and the live wham/usage body from the PRD, when readPool() runs, then that account has plan 'pro', a 'weekly' window with usedPercent 9, weeklyResetsAt = ISO of reset_at*1000, and exhausted false; with limit_reached true it reports exhausted true

Given a claude account whose usage body has five_hour and seven_day, when readPool() runs, then it returns '5-hour' and 'weekly' windows with resets_at as resetsAt; disabled and gemini accounts get no api-call and usageRead false

Given one account's api-call returns status_code 429, when readPool() runs, then only that account has error 'HTTP 429 from provider' and other accounts read normally; a hung api-call is aborted after 15 s under vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync
JSON.stringify of the returned snapshot never contains the management key or any access token string from the fixtures
Pure reset-first ranking: planPriorities

narrative.Action: PRD Decision 2 and work item 4 step 1. Create src/lib/cliproxy-routing.ts (module header: owns CLIProxy priority on eligible codex/claude accounts; never touches disabled or unreadable accounts) with exported pure planPriorities(accounts): Map<name, priority>. Per provider (codex, claude only): eligible = not disabled, usageRead, error null, weeklyResetsAt present. Do nothing when fewer than 2 eligible. Sort non-exhausted by weeklyResetsAt ascending, ties by lower weekly usedPercent, then authIndex ascending; priorities n*10 down to 10. Exhausted eligible => 0. Return only entries where desired !== account.priority (null counts as different). Import types from ./cliproxy-pool.js only.

items.title: Given two eligible codex accounts resetting in 1 day and 4 days, when planPriorities runs, then the 1-day account gets 20 and the 4-day account gets 10
Given equal reset times, when planPriorities runs, then the lower usedPercent ranks first, and with equal usedPercent the lower authIndex ranks first
Given three eligible accounts where one is exhausted, then the exhausted one gets 0 and the other two get 20 and 10
Given one eligible account plus one disabled and one with an error, then planPriorities returns an empty map (fewer than two eligible; disabled and errored accounts untouched)
Given accounts whose current priority already equals the desired value, then those names are absent from the returned map
Controller tick: refreshPool, readPoolSnapshot and the 5-minute timer gated on 2+ enabled accounts

narrative.Action: PRD work item 4 steps 2-4. In src/lib/cliproxy-routing.ts add getPoolSnapshot() (module variable), refreshPool() (readPool -> planPriorities -> setAccountPriority one at a time; update changed priorities in the snapshot; a failed PATCH logs '[cliproxy-routing] priority update failed for <name>' with the name only and leaves that account unchanged), readPoolSnapshot() (readPool, store, never calls setAccountPriority), and startCliproxyRoutingController(): first tick at 10 s, then every 5 min, tickInFlight guard like startCliproxyWatchdog. Each tick calls listPoolAccounts() first and calls refreshPool() only when codex or claude has 2+ non-disabled accounts; otherwise no usage reads. Errors are logged, never thrown. refreshPool is the only caller of setAccountPriority. Tests mock ./cliproxy-pool.js and use vi.useFakeTimers + vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync, no real waits.

Given listPoolAccounts reports one codex account and no claude accounts, when ticks fire, then readPool and setAccountPriority are never called

Given setAccountPriority rejects for one account, when refreshPool runs, then the other changes still apply, the snapshot keeps the old priority for the failed one, and the logged message contains the account name but no key or token
